Why do they exist?

Lots of reasons, but I'd put insecurity pretty high up on the list. Many people are fundamentally afraid because they find themselves cast adrift in a world that's sincerely mostly beyond their control. Rather than coming to terms with the fact that much of it is beyond their control and learning how to live with courage in the face of uncertainty, they double down on their efforts to control whatever little corner of the world they might be able to.

An odd little sidelight of the control thing that I've noticed - it seems to often be the case that those who seek to control others have a notable lack of control over themselves. I suspect that that's not a coincidence, though I'm not sure which is chicken and which is egg - whether they fail to control themselves because they're so focused on controlling others or if they focus on controlling others because they can't or won't control themselves.

A different aspect of insecurity that likely applies at least a good part of the time is the feeling that ones life is meaningless. People want to feel important and valuable, and for some at least, that's accomplished by wielding power. They convince themselves that they're meaningful because they have a measurable effect on other people. And it's likely that they're people who fear that they couldn't have that sort of effect otherwise - that if they simply talked to people and shared their thoughts or whatever, they'd be ignored. They have to force themselves on others in order to ensure that they have an effect.

And so on... I'm sure there are almost as many flimsy justifications for being power-hungry as there are power-hungry people.
